title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout & Go-live Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout and go-live planning. Discussed canary strategies, A/B testing, monitoring/alerting needs, cutover timing, rollback criteria, and security requirements (SOC2, VPC/KMS). Redwood will draft runbook and final canary plan; customer to share list of critical endpoints and schedule for maintenance window. SE to run targeted benchmark for 1k rps steady state and share latency/cost numbers.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-23
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Anita (Redwood CSM), Karen (Nimbus VP Eng), Devon (SRE), Priya (MLOps), Aaron (Security)

Auto-summary: Weekly POC sync to align on rollout and go-live plans. Lots of focus on canary vs A/B, monitoring SLIs, and security gating. Action items captured at end.

00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy holidays, we'll keep it tight — main agenda is rollout, canary plan, monitoring and any final security blockers. Marco will drive the bench stuff.
00:18 Karen: Thanks, yeah we want to make sure we have a clean cutover plan, minimal user impact. We're aiming for a phased roll next month, unsure about A/B vs canary.
00:30 Marco: Right, quick context — our last benchmark with the quantized model at 16k token context showed 95th p90 around 260 ms on the Dedicated config, but that was synthetic. We'll re-run steady state 1k rps to confirm.
00:48 Devon: When you say dedicated, is that the Redwood Dedicated pool? We need to compare cost and fallbacks to hosted during peak. Also, what about the KV cache behavior for short sessions — we saw some cold start spikes.
01:05 Sofia: Yep Dedicated is the reserved capacity, we'll include fallback to hosted API for overflow. The KV cache — Marco, can you explain the prefix cache behavior and warmup time?
01:14 Marco: Sure — the runtime does prefix/K-V caching, sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in notes — but practical impact is first few requests after a restart see higher latency until cache warms, usually ~60-90s for common prefixes. For canary we recommend pre-warm scripts that hit the common endpoints.
01:40 Priya: For canary vs A/B — our goal is to validate correctness for clinical triage flows. A/B might be riskier if the user experience differs, canary on small % of traffic seems safer. We also want quality monitoring tied to a prompt set so we can detect regressions.
02:05 Aaron: From security, SOC2 and VPC/KMS are gating items. We need audit logs, SAML SSO integration, and encryption with customer-managed KMS. Are these in scope for Private or Dedicated?
02:20 Sofia: All supported — Private is the full VPC/on-prem option with customer-managed KMS, Dedicated supports KMS integrations and audit logs as well. We'll attach the security pack docs.
02:35 Karen: Good. On monitoring, we need a runbook: who escalates, what thresholds trigger rollback, and automated rollback or manual?
02:45 Marco: The typical pattern we recommend: start with a canary cohort (1-5% traffic) for 24-72 hours. Metrics: latency P95/P99, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, qualitative quality signals (prompt evals). Rollback criteria: sustained P99 > X ms or error rate > Y% for 10 minutes. We can make it auto or manual; customers often choose manual for first cutover.
03:12 Devon: What's X and Y? We should set concrete thresholds. Our existing SLA for other services is P99 < 700 ms and errors < 0.5%. Can we map to token latency?
03:25 Marco: We'll propose thresholds after the final bench. From prior runs, P99 was around 380 ms on Dedicated for typical prompts. Suggest P99 threshold at 750 ms and error rate 1% as conservative.
03:40 Priya: Also want retention and logging for 90 days for evaluation data; does Redwood store prompts? We need to avoid PHI storage.
03:52 Sofia: Redwood does not persist customer prompt content unless configured; for Private there is full control. We'll note best practices: token redaction, on-the-fly masking, and streaming to your datastore for evals.
04:10 Karen: About canary cohort selection — we want to exclude paying customers and internal users. We'll start with internal beta then 1% of external traffic.
04:25 Marco: Sounds good. For A/B we usually do model vs model comparisons with randomized routing and a small percentage; but because of quality sensitivity you probably prefer canary with a deterministic fallback policy.
04:38 Aaron: On the compliance side, need to confirm KMS key rotation and HSM support. Priya, do we need FIPS?
04:46 Priya: Not FIPS right now but HSM/KMS with rotation is in scope.
05:00 Marco: I'll include the KMS/HSM notes in the runbook. Also, we'll add the list of smoke tests: auth flows, top 10 endpoints, end-to-end latency check, and model output sanity checks.
05:20 Karen: Cutover timing — we propose the weekend of Jan 9th maintenance window. Does that align with Redwood support availability?
05:30 Anita: Yes Redwood can staff a cutover window around that date; we'll assign on-call SE to monitor.
05:38 Devon: For rollback mechanics, what's easiest? DNS switch, traffic routing at the LB, or can Redwood do model variant routing?
05:45 Sofia: We have routing policies at the gateway level that can shift traffic by percentage, and can also route by region or token cost. For a full rollback it's easiest to shift traffic back to the previous model variant via the routing API — near-instant.
06:05 Karen: Nice. For canary duration, if we do 24 hours and metrics are green, we can ramp to 25% then 100% over next 48 hours?
06:16 Marco: Agree. Ramp plan: 1% -> 5% (24 hrs) -> 25% (24 hrs) -> 100% (24-48 hrs) with checks at each step.
06:29 Priya: We need automated alerts in PagerDuty for our SRE and Redwood ops channel. Devon, can you set that up?
06:36 Devon: Yes, I'll provision a PD escalation with separate channels for canary vs production.
06:42 Sofia: On monitoring, we'll propose dashboards: per-route latency P50/P90/P99, error rates, token usage, cost per 1k tokens, and a quality dashboard for prompt set regressions.
07:00 Karen: Also want runbook entries for degraded performance: who restarts pods, who escalates to Redwood, and when we flip to hosted fallback.
07:12 Marco: We'll add explicit steps: pre-checks, smoke test script, cutover playbook, rollback playbook, contact list & pager codes.
07:25 Priya: About evaluation — we asked Redwood to run prompt-based evals every hour during the canary. Is that feasible?
07:33 Marco: Yes, we can schedule continuous evals against our stored prompt set and surface score deltas. We'll include baseline metrics in the dashboard.
07:45 Karen: Cost question: during rollout, what are cost implications of parallel runs for A/B?
07:52 Sofia: A/B doubles token costs for the split traffic; canary is incremental. We can recommend using smaller quantized model for A/B if you want to reduce cost, but that may affect quality. We'll include cost estimates in the runbook.
08:10 Devon: Any third-party monitoring integrations? We use Datadog and Splunk.
08:18 Marco: Redwood supports metrics export to Datadog and logs to your Splunk via forwarders; we'll provide config snippets.
08:28 Aaron: Legal/procurement — we need a signed addendum for Dedicated capacity and ILP terms. Who handles that?
08:35 Anita: I'll loop in our sales ops and legal. We'll share a draft addendum and pricing.
08:44 Karen: Can we get a final performance run this week? We need numbers to finalize thresholds.
08:51 Marco: Yes I'll run a steady-state 1k rps bench with realistic token distributions and share the spreadsheet. Expect results by Sunday.
09:00 Priya: For canary evaluation, our SLIs list: P95 latency, P99 latency, 90th quantile token cost, error rate, and a quality score from prompt evals.
09:12 Sofia: We'll map those to dashboard widgets and automated alerts.
09:20 Karen: Anything else?
09:25 Devon: On the preload/warm scripts — can Redwood provide examples?
09:28 Marco: Yes we'll send pre-warm scripts and a short guide: hit top 50 endpoints, warm KV, health endpoints.
09:36 Sofia: Quick recap then action items. Redwood will draft runbook, benchmark results, pre-warm scripts, and monitoring dashboards. Nimbus to provide endpoints, traffic numbers, and confirm cutover window.
09:50 Karen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone, we'll review runbook next week.
10:00 Sofia: Thanks all, Happy Holidays, meeting adjourned.

Post-call notes (auto): some transcription glitches: "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "p90 around 260 ms" variances noted. References to shared artifacts: Redwood runbook draft (link to be sent), performance spreadsheet (to be shared), security docs (Redwood security pack link).
